name: satyalens-real-world-test

source.title: SMS PHISHING DATASET FOR MACHINE LEARNING AND PATTERN RECOGNITION
source.licence: CC BY 4.0 (as stated on the Mendeley Data dataset page)
source.attribution: Mishra, S., Soni, D. (2022). SMS PHISHING DATASET FOR MACHINE LEARNING AND PATTERN RECOGNITION. Mendeley Data, V1. doi:10.17632/f45bkkt8pr.1
source.collection_method_as_described: Images obtained from the Internet converted to text with Python code; labelled by source and cleaned.

label_basis: Labels are the source authors' published labels; they were not re-annotated by this project.

derived_columns.near_duplicate_cluster: skeleton_text() equality cluster; derived, NOT a source campaign id
derived_columns.heuristic_topic: keyword heuristic ('financial'/'other'); a reporting aid, NOT ground truth

limitations: Domain mismatch: messages are largely UK/Singapore SMS from c. 2000s-2010s (a systematic review describes the dataset as a partial clone of the UCI SMS Spam Collection), not Indian financial communications like the SatyaLens use case.
'smishing' in the source includes premium-rate, prize and subscription scams, not only financial/bank fraud; 'ham' is mostly personal chat with few genuine bank alerts.
No campaign/group identifiers in the source; near-duplicate clusters are derived from text.
Labels were not independently verified; some label noise is likely (OCR-derived text).
Encoding damage in the source (e.g. the pound sign appears as '?').
No message categories in the source; heuristic_topic is keyword-based.
